known_link: The gene cluster from MBT84_08725 to MBT84_08905 are confirmed to be induced by catechol. Only the biosynthetic proteins of this cluster were mostly significantly up regulated in catechol-grown cultures, which provided validation of the involvement of this BGC in the observed change in bioactivity induced by catechol. To confirm that BGC4 was indeed responsible for the production of the angucycline glycosides, we knocked down transcription of the gene for the KSβ (MBT84_08755) of the minimal PKS using CRISPR-dCas9 interference. Metabolomics analysis revealed that the production of the angucycline glycosides was significantly reduced when the expression of KSβ was inhibited.

known_link: The sponge Mycale hentscheli is the source of the polyketide Mycalamide A. Since there is a close correlation between the module architecture of a polyketide synthase and the polyketide structure, assumptions about the core BGC are possible if the structure is known and vice versa. The mycalamide biosynthetic gene cluster (myc) was identified in the metagenome of a sponge sample known to contain mycalamide. The module architecture is in good agreement with the mycalamide structure. The assignment of the biosynthetic gene cluster to mycalamide was facilitated by the fact that mycalamide belongs to the pederin-family molecules for which very similar gene clusters were already known.
